label: class_b_07_math_01
text: Hello, everyone. I hope we can have fun once\nagain today for our last class together.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_02
text: Last time we learned about probability, using\nmove accuracy as an example.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_03
text:
Probability is quite an interesting subject. Did
you know that, in a class with 40 students, there
is a 90 percent chance that two of them will have
the same birthday?[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_04
text: This is true even despite the fact that there are\nover 300 days each year. Isn’t that remarkable?[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_05
text: But let’s move on to today’s topic before we\nget swept along with probability again.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_06
text: I’ve been teaching you all how to calculate\ndamage in this class using examples like type\r\nmatchups, critical hits, stat boosts, and the like.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_07
text: All of these variables are multiplied together to\ncalculate damage dealt to an opponent.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_08
text: However, did you know that there is an even\nsimpler way to increase the damage of your\r\nPokémon’s moves?[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_09
text: All you have to do is have your Pokémon use\na move it shares a type with![VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_10
text: If a Rock-type Pokémon uses the Rock-type move\nStone Edge, the move’s base power of 100 is\r\nmultiplied by 1.5 to become 150.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_11
text: Ground and Rock may seem like similar types,\nbut if a Ground-type Pokémon uses Stone Edge,\r\nthe move’s power will remain 100.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_12
text: Supereffective moves and critical hits also add\nmultipliers on to this little numerical increase,\r\nso it most certainly must not be taken lightly.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_13
text: Let me ask you a question to see if you\nunderstand what I’m talking about here.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_14
text:
Say you have a move with a power of 100. If a
Pokémon that shares a type with this move
uses it and hits an opponent that is weak to
that type, what happens to that move’s power?[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_select_01
text: Its power becomes 150

label: class_b_07_select_02
text: Its power becomes 200

label: class_b_07_select_03
text: Its power becomes 300

label: class_b_07_math_answer_01
text: Close! But a power of 150 would only take into\naccount the multiplier of 1.5 resulting from the\r\nPokémon sharing a type with the move.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_answer_02
text: Close! But a power of 200 would only take into\naccount the doubling effect of using a move\r\nthat is super effective against an opponent.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_answer_03
text: You did that calculation all in your head? Well\ndone, [VAR 0x0100(0000)]![VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_15
text: First, using a move that shares a type with its user\nmultiplies the move’s base power of 100 by 1.5,\r\nmaking the power 150![VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_16
text: The fact that the opponent is weak to the move’s\ntype then doubles that power from 150 to 300![VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_17
text: The original power of the move ends up being\ntripled! Isn’t that amazing?[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_18
text:
What’s more, if a Pokémon Terastallizes and its
Tera Type matches one of its original types, then
the bonus it gets for using a move of that same
type increases from 1.5 to 2![VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_19
text: Of course, being able to use a lot of moves with\ndifferent types is great as well. That’s one way\r\nyou can surprise your opponent.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_20
text: In the end, your own innate characteristics are\nwhat will really let you shine the most.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_21
text: Bear in mind that this is true for both humans and\nPokémon.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_22
text: It sure would make me happy if you could take\nthose words to heart![VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_23
text: But I suppose I should really have shared this\nbasic advice right from our first lesson.\c\nMy apologies...[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_24
text: And just like that, class is over. The last of our\ntime together flew by in the blink of an eye.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_25
text: It was so much fun to be able to teach all you\neager students about numbers.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]

label: class_b_07_math_26
text: Next class will be our fun final exam! Be sure to\nreview the material well in preparation.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
